title: YAML
subtitle: Tools, personas, execution profiles and tool schemas are YAML in my estate, compiled and hash-pinned rather than parsed at runtime.

stats.label: lines of schema validating every persona
lines of catalog, personas, groundings and profiles
multi-action MCP tools on the control surface

lede: Agent Swarm rests on one idea of mine, that tools are the platform, and I wanted adding a tool or an agent class to be a declaration with no new code. The tools are YAML documents of four kinds, each with a Rust dispatcher. Every tool must ship with golden fixtures that pin its behaviour and attack fixtures that try to break it, such as an injection attempt against a shell template, and the build fails for a tool without them. See Tools are the platform. Personas are YAML too: each names a tool subset, a policy, a workspace and a container or execution profile, and a schema validates every one at load time.
quote: I use declarative configuration to make platforms extensible and keep them strict: every declaration is validated, tested or compiled before it takes effect.
evidence: Declarative tool and agent definition: 40 tools declared as YAML documents of four kinds, each with golden and attack fixtures the build enforces.
Schema validation: a 545-line schema validating every persona at load time, over about 12,000 lines of catalog, personas, groundings and profiles.
Code generation from schemas: 18 multi-action MCP tools whose dispatch code is generated from YAML schemas at build time.
author: Corey James
